open_points.subject: configuration-file re-read security
open_points.text: A17 says "Here and in rule 2 the path is opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any of them, and the checks and the read use that one opened file", while A16 says "Exactly four checks apply to a re-read" and "Every other field of the configuration, and every other start check, applies only at a restart."
open_points.question: On a per-request token-list re-read, must the configuration file still pass A17's no-symlink, regular-file, ownership and permission checks, or only A16's four checks?
options: Apply all A17 file-security checks on every re-read
Apply only A16's four checks after startup
Keep the originally opened configuration file and never reopen its path
open_points.default_guess: Apply all A17 file-security checks on every re-read.

open_points.subject: credential-file decoding
open_points.text: "its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value" and "holds an empty value or a control character"
open_points.question: Exactly which trailing byte sequence is removed, how many occurrences are removed, and which Unicode characters count as control characters?
options: Remove one final LF only and reject Unicode control-category characters
Remove one final LF or CRLF and reject ASCII C0 plus DEL
Strip all trailing line endings and use the HTTP field-value validity rules
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one final LF, removing a preceding CR with it, then reject ASCII C0 characters and DEL.

open_points.subject: service-instance selection at startup
open_points.text: "at most one selected instance per service, by its manifest instance name" and "The instance of every service is the one the installation selects"
open_points.question: What happens at startup when the configuration repeats a service selection, selects an unknown service or instance, or the selected instance cannot be read from the configured manifest revision?
options: Refuse kernel startup
Start, treating that service as having no selected instance
Start but preserve the invalid selection so each proposal or send reports an instance error
open_points.default_guess: Refuse duplicate selections, but start with an unknown or unreadable selection treated as unavailable to that service.

open_points.subject: service credential configuration cardinality
open_points.text: "at most one credential for each service it gives one"
open_points.question: How is a configuration containing two credential entries for the same service handled, and does equality of their contents change the result?
options: Refuse startup whenever the service appears twice
Accept identical duplicates but refuse differing duplicates
Use the last entry
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup whenever the service appears twice.

open_points.subject: data-directory privacy
open_points.text: "The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise."
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission conditions define "private" for the data directory, its subdirectories and its files, and are ACLs or other users' execute permissions included?
options: Kernel-user ownership and no group/other permission bits on every object
Only the root data directory must be kernel-owned and mode 0700
Require effective inaccessibility, including ACL checks
open_points.default_guess: Require kernel-user ownership and no group or other permission bits on every directory and file.

open_points.subject: data-directory root handling
open_points.text: "At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory" and "Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links"
open_points.question: May the data-directory path itself be a symbolic link, may the kernel create a missing directory, and which privacy checks occur before creating the lock or other files?
options: Require a pre-existing non-symlink directory and validate it before creating anything
Create a missing directory securely but reject a symlink root
Permit a symlink root if its resolved directory is private
open_points.default_guess: Require a pre-existing non-symlink directory and validate it before creating the lock.

open_points.subject: global store order
open_points.text: "Activation M09 and FlowActivation M18 records are identified by their position in the store's one order of records" and "one record ever has two orders"
open_points.question: What exactly is the single store position, and what order is assigned to multiple records created in one transaction?
options: One global monotonically increasing sequence with an explicitly fixed within-call record order
SQLite insertion order independently within each table
The transaction position is shared by all records written in that transaction
open_points.default_guess: Use one global monotonically increasing sequence and assign positions in the normative write order of each store call.

open_points.subject: request serialization order
open_points.text: "Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive"
open_points.question: What defines arrival order when multiple MCP requests are received concurrently or in the same transport event?
options: Order in which complete request messages are accepted by the MCP server
Order in which request processing tasks acquire the writer
Transport connection order followed by message order within each connection
open_points.default_guess: Order complete request messages by the MCP server's single receive sequence.

open_points.subject: store-call atomic boundary
open_points.text: "Every change is one call to the store module and one transaction inside it"
open_points.question: Which related mutations constitute one indivisible change—for example a function conclusion, its values and NodeExecution, approval creation plus waiting state, and run status or waiting-point updates?
options: Each normative transition and all records it requires are one store call
Each individual record mutation is a separate store call
The entire request, including all node advances, is one store call
open_points.default_guess: Treat each normative transition of one element as one store call, atomically including its records, values, waiting points and resulting run state.

open_points.subject: late symbolic-link detection
open_points.text: A18 rule 2 says a link found later "makes that store call fail with nothing written", while rule 3 says a failed store call may leave "a published file no record names".
open_points.question: If a store call publishes a file and subsequently encounters a symbolic link, must the published file be removed, or is the orphan-file exception allowed?
options: Preflight every path so a symlink failure writes and publishes nothing
Remove any file published by that call before reporting failure
Allow the published orphan despite the phrase "nothing written"
open_points.default_guess: Preflight all relevant paths so a symlink failure publishes nothing.

open_points.subject: content-addressed file collision
open_points.text: "Equal bytes are stored once" and "a completed file a record names is never overwritten"
open_points.question: What happens when a file already exists at a digest-derived location but its bytes or size differ from the bytes now being published under that digest?
options: Compare existing content and stop with an integrity failure on mismatch
Assume SHA-256 collisions cannot occur and reuse the existing file
Store colliding content under an additional identity
open_points.default_guess: Compare the existing bytes and stop the kernel with an integrity failure on mismatch.

open_points.subject: orphan spool files of unfinished runs
open_points.text: Startup removes "temporary files, value bytes no record names ... and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool"; A13 says unnamed failed-attempt files may remain "until that spool is removed ... or a later write to the same position replaces them".
open_points.question: After restart, do unnamed files in an unfinished run's spool count toward `spool_run_bytes_max`, get removed, or remain ignored until their exact position is reused?
options: Keep them and count their bytes toward the run ceiling
Remove every spool file not named by a record
Keep them but exclude them from the run ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Keep them and count them toward `spool_run_bytes_max` until replaced or the spool is removed.

open_points.subject: retry eligibility of waiting elements
open_points.text: A13 says a mapped pass runs elements that have "no concluded record and do not wait" and "a concluded element is never executed again", while `service_unreachable` writes a NodeExecution and A14 later resends that element.
open_points.question: Which NodeExecution statuses make an element permanently concluded, and which leave it retryable despite its concluded attempt record?
options: Only terminal success, failure and skip statuses conclude the element; `service_unreachable` and unresolved `outcome_unknown` remain waiting
Every NodeExecution concludes the element, with resume creating a distinct retry exception
Only `service_unreachable` remains retryable; `outcome_unknown` can move only through resolution
open_points.default_guess: Treat `service_unreachable` and unresolved `outcome_unknown` as concluded attempts but not concluded elements; all other listed statuses conclude the element.

open_points.subject: guard comparison
open_points.text: "A guarded edge delivers only when its guard port's value equals its guard value."
open_points.question: What equality relation is used for guard values, especially for JSON numbers such as `1` and `1.0`, objects with different member order, and strings with canonically equivalent Unicode?
options: Equality of RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes
JSON data-model equality with numeric values compared mathematically
Type-sensitive structural equality without Unicode normalization
open_points.default_guess: Use equality of RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes.

open_points.subject: multi-output node commitment
open_points.text: "An element that does not succeed keeps no output" and, only for mapped aggregate lists, "Every delivered list ... is measured before any of them is delivered or written".
open_points.question: For an ordinary node with several outputs, must all outputs pass schema and size checks before any output is stored or delivered, or may earlier outputs remain when a later output fails?
options: Validate and measure every output before storing or delivering any
Process outputs in port-name order and discard references if a later output fails
Allow successfully processed outputs to remain produced
open_points.default_guess: Validate and measure all outputs first, then atomically record and deliver them only if every output passes.

open_points.subject: startup recovery advancement
open_points.text: State 0 says "a run advances one node at a time, inside the request that moves it"; A13 says "A run advances only inside a request" but adds "except the start-up recovery of A14 rule 5", which advances runs before the surface opens.
open_points.question: Is startup recovery an accepted exception to the earlier invariant, or must it only reconstruct state and wait for a later request before executing or sending anything?
options: Startup recovery may advance runnable nodes as A14 states
Startup recovery may reconstruct records but cannot execute nodes
Recovery must be represented as an internal request so the earlier invariant remains literal
open_points.default_guess: Treat startup recovery as an explicit kernel-actor exception that may advance runnable nodes before the surface opens.
